_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform — the EPW EnergyPlus `any` mutation vocabulary and the reference implementation that exercises it. An EnergyPlus weather file is 8 fixed header lines followed by 8,760 comma-separated hourly records, so the already-linked `csv` crate is registered here under a distinct id/capability for the RECORD half only (per the wave 7 fleet brief's oracle-registration gotcha: reusing the shared csv-rfc4180 entry would fail the contract with oracle-capability-mismatch, and would also misrepresent what csv actually validates for this format). `csv` is genuinely independent for the 35-column hourly records; the 8 header lines (LOCATION, DESIGN CONDITIONS, TYPICAL/EXTREME PERIODS, GROUND TEMPERATURES, HOLIDAYS/DAYLIGHT SAVINGS, COMMENTS 1, COMMENTS 2, DATA PERIODS) are EnergyPlus-specific grammar that no third-party crate on crates.io validates -- `epw-rs` was surveyed and rejected: it is alpha-quality and read-only (no writer), which would rule out differential coverage anyway. Record-kind mutations (`no-mutation`, `insert-record`, `remove-record`, `set-record-field`) are typed `@mode-differential`: `csv` genuinely reads AND writes that half. Header-kind mutations (`set-snapshot`, `set-location`, `set-design-conditions`, `set-typical-extreme-periods`, `set-ground-temperatures`, `set-holidays-dst`, `set-comments-1`, `set-comments-2`, `set-data-periods`) are typed `@mode-property`: the oracle module writes the header bytes itself (hand-rolled, independent of the subject crate) and reads them back with `csv`'s generic comma-grid reader for structural evidence only, never claiming an independent second PRODUCER for header semantics it does not have.

oracles.rationale: The reference RFC 4180-shaped CSV reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem, read/written with `has_headers(false)` and `flexible(true)` exactly as the sibling `csv-rfc4180-mutate` entry does. Genuinely authoritative for EPW's 8,760 comma-separated hourly records (35 columns each, real per-record information the way this subset's own schema already models it) — used both as the independent PRODUCER for record-kind mutations and as the independent READER for the semantic projection. It carries no knowledge of EnergyPlus header grammar (LOCATION/DESIGN CONDITIONS/GROUND TEMPERATURES/DATA PERIODS field meanings), so header-kind mutations are registered against this same oracle for its reading role only and typed `@mode-property` rather than `@mode-differential` in the case's feature file — see that file's own description for the full honesty accounting. `epw-rs` (the only EPW-specific crate found) was surveyed and NOT registered: alpha-quality and read-only, which the fleet brief's §6 rules out for a differential producer.

comparisonProfiles.description: EPW documents compared by the 8 header lines plus the full ordered record grid. `location` and `dataPeriods` are compared as typed objects; the four remaining EnergyPlus-specific header blocks (design conditions, typical/extreme periods, ground temperatures, holidays/DST) plus the two comment lines are compared as retained verbatim strings, matching this subset's own lossless schema (`../../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🦀️component.rs`) field for field. Record order is normative (EPW rows have no identity beyond position, same convention this subset's own diff module documents) and every one of a record's 35 columns is compared verbatim -- no numeric coercion, since the schema stores every column as `String` specifically to avoid the `20.0`-vs-`20` formatting hazard. No key is ignored: this subset's own codec always emits CRLF with a trailing terminator and never chooses between alternate serializations, so there is no producer-freedom axis for this profile to except the way `semantic-tabular-v1`'s `lineTerminator`/`quoteStyle` keys do for RFC 4180.
